quest.title: The Chi of Yore
quest.description: It seems Mt. Qingce is hiding some secrets...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Liyue Shrine of Depths Key x1

dialogues.speaker: Incomplete Writing
dialogues.text: "...Rex Lapis overcame the Chi, but the Chi could not perish in its entirety. Thus did Rex Lapis conquer each of its facets in turn: its spirit was bound in the <color=#00E1FFFF>north</color>, its bones were pinned in the <color=#00E1FFFF>south-east</color>, its flesh was incarcerated in the <color=#00E1FFFF>north-west</color>, its soul was fettered in the <color=#00E1FFFF>north-east</color>, and its form was crushed in the <color=#00E1FFFF>south-west</color>..."

dialogues.speaker: Incomplete Writing
dialogues.text: "...Its bones pierced, its spirit faded, its form and soul both decimated... still did its flesh survive..."

dialogues.speaker: Incomplete Writing
dialogues.text: Here stands this statue, to <color=#00E1FFFF>watch in each direction</color>: the <color=#00E1FFFF>wind-swept ruin</color>, the <color=#00E1FFFF>snow-capped peak</color>, the <color=#00E1FFFF>adepti's abode</color>, and the <color=#00E1FFFF>city of Liyue</color>...

dialogues.speaker: Yan'er
dialogues.text: Agh, what terrible luck...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Yan'er
dialogues.text: Oh, Traveler. You've come at the right time. I was just doing some, uh, research.

dialogues.speaker: Yan'er
dialogues.text: You know the name of this place, right? Qingce Village?

dialogues.speaker: Yan'er
dialogues.text: So, how do I say this... Do you understand what "Qingce" means?

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: Well, its origin and hidden meaning, of course. Should have known you weren't the cultured sort...

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: Do you know about the Chi? According to legend, the Chi was a dragon-like monster that once forcibly occupied this place.

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: When Rex Lapis — or Morax — defeated it, the Chi's body twisted into rock, its blood turned into water, and its scales became the terraced fields.

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: And in times long past, the word "Chi" also used to mean "Qingce."

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: And, through my long, earnest and rigorous research...

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: I believe that the Chi's corpse may still be on this mountain.

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: Hmph, don't be so dismissive. Haven't you noticed the giant trees growing in this area? Don't you think that they're a lot larger and sturdier than elsewhere?

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: The locals call these Blood-Fed Trees. They believe that these trees grew by absorbing the Chi's blood, and that the area where they grew are the Chi's Eyes.

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: And indeed, the growth of these trees is abnormal.

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: Even if it were not truly the corpse of that monster, there must be something incredible underground...

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: Of course! How could I give up on something so... researchable?

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: I say that, but the truth is that I don't have a lot of leads.

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: It is, after all, an antediluvian legend. It's likely that barely anyone even remembers the legend anymore.

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: After all the effort I put into finding these ruins, thinking that I might be able to find something in here...

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: ...It turned out that there's a <color=#00E1FFFF>Ruin Hunter</color> standing guard inside. That's why I said that my luck was terrible.

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: I'd really like to go in and have a look, but it's far too dangerous. I'll probably wait until it leaves before giving this a go.

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: Are you looking to go inside and explore, by any chance? Not that I'd stop you, no, but...

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: Please be mindful of your safety. This might be the clue to some treasure, but it's just a legend in the end. Don't pay it too much mind.

choices.text: And what would the corpse be used for?

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: Uses? For a monster's corpse? Do you even have any idea...

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: Ahem! Do you even know how valuable it is for research?

response.speaker: Yan'er
response.text: That's it? "It's pretty unique"? So uncultured...

dialogues.speaker: Yan'er
dialogues.text: This way, I can... Whoa! Y—You're still here?

dialogues.speaker: Yan'er
dialogues.text: I'm going to rest for a while, and then... then I'll be going.

dialogues.speaker: Yan'er
dialogues.text: Take care of yourself now, and don't push yourself too much. For all we know, it really is just a legend.

talks.objective: Ask the locals of Qingce Village about the fragments

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: I have this fragment...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: A fragment of...? Found something curious, have you? Let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Heh... No wonder you can't make head or tail of it. This isn't writing on here — it's a drawing.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Long, long ago, before writing was invented, people recorded events with pictures.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Look, this symbol here depicts the Chi — a legendary beast. It looks like the full symbol must have been very large and complex, this is only part of it. But it's enough for me to recognize it by.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: My guess is that this depicts the battle between the Geo Lord and the Chi. But it's hard to be more specific from just this one piece.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If you had all the pieces, could you make sense of it?

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Oh, I don't know about that. No guarantee.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: But what I can guarantee is that without all the pieces, I certainly can't make sense of it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Watch me, I'll find the rest in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Hehe... So much enthusiasm. I like that about young people.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Given what this fragment is showing, I'd say that if you really want to find the other fragments, here's what you should do...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: According to the legend of the Geo Lord and the Chi, the battle took place at a <color=#00E1FFFF>great height</color>. So you could try your luck on the mountaintops around here.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Beyond that, there are many traces of the battle in this area. <color=#00E1FFFF>Ruins</color> would be a sensible place to look.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: In every conflict there is a losing side. The legend tells that after defeating the Chi, the Geo Lord instructed our forebears to erect <color=#00E1FFFF>Geo Statues</color> to crush the Chi's remaining power.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: I'd guess you would have a higher chance of finding things to do with the Chi in places with lots of <color=#00E1FFFF>Geo Statues</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: For example, there are many <color=#00E1FFFF>Geo Statues</color> erected <color=#00E1FFFF>west</color> of Qingce Village. It's said that's the very spot where the Geo Lord crushed the Chi... Maybe you'll strike lucky over that way.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Once you've found all the fragments, bring them to me. I'll be waiting right here.

talks.objective: Ask Granny Ruoxin about the fragments
Head to Qingce Village and ask the locals about the fragments

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Hello, and welcome to Qingce Village.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you do?

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: You found a hidden chamber behind a waterfall?

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: What did you find inside?

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Nothing special, you say... That's good, that's good... best there be nothing special...

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Haha, look at you two, covered in dust from head to toe... I'm sure you two had quite the unpleasant adventure in there too.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Here, take these. Go buy something nice to eat, and rest your legs a bit.

choices.text: Um, we didn't do that much...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, Granny, we didn't do anything at all!

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Oh, listen to yourselves. Didn't you help us chase those Treasure Hoarders away from our village?

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Allow me to give these to you as a token of appreciation, on behalf of everyone in Qingce Village.

choices.text: We don't take payment if the work's not done...
We found a whole bunch of Treasure Hoarders outside.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Treasure Hoarders? Did you chase them off?

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Those low-down, no-good crooks, always skulking about. They're so annoying. It's high time someone taught them a lesson.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: So there was nothing special inside, you say? That's good, that's good... best there be nothing special...

talks.objective: Head to the ruin to search for fragments

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Paimon can't make any sense of this at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't tell if it's supposed to be a drawing, or writing, or... some other kind of thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe the locals will have an idea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's ask around in Qingce Village.

talks.objective: Go to the highest point of Qingce Village to search for fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That makes three fragments we've found. And it looks like they match up...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So we just need to put them together, and... Nope. Still makes no sense to Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess we do need to ask the locals after all, huh...

talks.objective: Search for fragments near the Geo Statues

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...So that's it? Aw, but what about our monster corpse? And our treasure?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Surely a place this big can't be completely empty? And think of all the effort we've put into this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Shall we give it another once-over, just to be sure?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have some fragments...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Let's see now... Why, these fragments all fit together.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: See here, this is the symbol for a Chi, and this Chi was defeated in a major battle.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Afterward, it was pinned down in a deep place.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's a Chi?

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: In the legends, the Chi was a dragon-like monster, and Mt. Qingce was once its lair.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: When Rex Lapis — or Morax — defeated it, the Chi's body twisted into rock, its blood turned into water, and its scales became the terraced fields.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Do you see those sturdy trees near Qingce Village? Those are Blood-Fed Trees, said to have been nourished by the blood of the Chi.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: But a legend is a legend. After all, who would be able to find traces of the Chi today?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened after that?

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: After that... in order to seal the corpse of the Chi and prevent it from endangering the world again, water was used to seal its corpse, and treasures were used to pin it in the center of the vault...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Hmm, the rest of it is illegible.

choices.text: Does the Chi's corpse still exist?

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: I'm afraid that other than Rex Lapis, no one else knows the answer to that question.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: So, young one, do you think that the things recorded on these three fragments are true?

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Well, it's not a bad thing for a young person to bumble around a bit.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: But if you really want to pursue your search according to the content of these fragments, then I say that the place you're looking for must have something to do with <color=#00E1FFFF>water</color>.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Not only that, but it must also be <color=#00E1FFFF>water</color> whose <color=#00E1FFFF>entrance</color> can be blocked.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Let me think... Come to think of it, there is a sizable waterfall northwest of Qingce Village. I wonder if it has something to do with that vault...

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Well, that's all I know. As for the rest, you'll have to mull it over yourself.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Haha, young one... you can't resist the thought of treasure, can you?

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: So, do you think that the things recorded on these three fragments are true?

talks.objective: Find a way into the vault

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: You're back. So, did you find anything?

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Hahaha. It's alright, not to worry, there is nothing wrong with a bit of extra running around while you're young enough to handle it.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Here, these are for you. You've been out and about all day. Go buy something nice to eat, and rest your legs a bit.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: So there was nothing inside... That's good, that's good...

choices.text: We found a whole bunch of Treasure Hoarders outside.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Treasure Hoarders? Did you chase them off?

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Those low-down, no-good crooks, always skulking about. They're so annoying. It's high time someone taught them a lesson.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: And there was... nothing inside? Hahaha, no matter, no matter at all. there is nothing wrong with a bit of extra running around while you're young enough to handle it.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Here, these are for you. You've been out and about all day. Go buy something nice to eat, and rest your legs a bit.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: So there was nothing inside... That's good, that's good...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These three lines are so hard to read... But they did mention that "three Chi Trees were used to subdue it..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chi Trees... Um, are they referring to <color=#00E1FFFF>some sort of tree</color>?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's look around, and look out for <color=#00E1FFFF>trees</color>. Who knows, we might find some clues!

talks.objective: Head to Qingce Village and report to Granny Ruoxin

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: The Chi remains a shadow that haunts us. To think that someone would have designs on its corpse!

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: ...Well, I can only hope that it's just that bunch of two-bit crooks. But if there truly is something down there...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: ...Ah, Geo Lord, protect us...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So after all that running around, we still didn't find anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Chi, the treasure, it's all just a legend!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, it's weird. Why did the village chief granny seem so happy about that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so that's it? But we found nothing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let have another look, just to be sure. We've come this far... we gotta have something to show for it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those Treasure Hoarders look real scary. Paimon remembers that Qingce Village is nearby...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go there, find someone and tell them about this. It's best that they be on guard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We won't let these bad guys get their way!

talks.objective: Head to Qingce Village and ask the village chief about the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Investigation Log
dialogues.text: "...studies show that these ruins date back to very ancient times indeed; they are older than the collective age of all the elderly residents of Qingce Village put together."

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Investigation Log
dialogues.text: "In other words, we find these ruins to be entirely generic, indistinguishable in substance from other ruins."

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Investigation Log
dialogues.text: "Yet despite their generic nature, the majority of these ruins contain treasure. Though driven out by the Ruin Hunters here, the allure of the treasure contained within will be sure to see the Treasure Hoarders return."

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Investigation Log
dialogues.text: "According to Chang the Ninth, who lives on the mountain, there was once an old town below. Once it was destroyed there was... what was it... something that was sealed away underground. Something to do with some kind of golden stone..."

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Investigation Log
dialogues.text: "But he's a destitute scholar who loves citing the classics and going off on tangents. Added to the fact that I drank a lot with him to get the conversation going, I can't remember what he said very clearly. I think the crux of it was that it had something to do with some golden stone and Ruin Hunters... That old man really can drink a lot."

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Investigation Log
dialogues.text: "The heavy drinking and the bitterly cold wind have left my head feeling like it's been bashed about by a bunch of hilichurls."

dialogues.speaker: Ruins Investigation Log
dialogues.text: "Actually now I think about it... Maybe I really did get attacked by hilichurls on my way down the mountain last night? I can't remember for sure... My head sure does hurt though. Better get myself to a doctor in Liyue Harbor before thinking any more about these ruins."

dialogues.speaker: Incomplete Writing
dialogues.text: "With the evil serpent gone from Qingce, the magic formula that subdued it was no longer in effect. ..."

dialogues.speaker: Incomplete Writing
dialogues.text: "...But the serpent did not perish, and its foul blood congealed within the earth and formed stone, poisoning the world..."

dialogues.speaker: Incomplete Writing
dialogues.text: "...Thus three statues were used to subdue it..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Just three lines and Paimon's head is hurting. Why are all Liyue's stories written like this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But anyway, that bit that goes <color=#00E1FFFF>"foul blood something something formed stone"</color>... does that mean there's <color=#00E1FFFF>strange stone</color> around here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's take a look around at the <color=#00E1FFFF>stones</color> around here and see if we can find some leads.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The people of Qingce are really friendly. Hehe, guess we didn't come all this way for nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, don't you feel like that granny was too happy about all this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can Paimon put this... Is kicking the Treasure Hoarders out something to be that happy about?

dialogues.speaker: Master Lu
dialogues.text: Take a look at this fragment?

dialogues.speaker: Master Lu
dialogues.text: Fragment? What fragment, is it from some toy that was broken?

dialogues.speaker: Master Lu
dialogues.text: I have never encountered a fragment of this kind before.

dialogues.speaker: Master Lu
dialogues.text: Perhaps you should ask the village chief. Perhaps she might know something.

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: Can you read this fragment?

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: A fragment? Hmm... No, I can't read it.

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: As a matter of fact, I've never seen one in my life.

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: You should go ask Granny Ruoxin, she might know something about it.

dialogues.speaker: Zhi
dialogues.text: Know anything about this fragment?

dialogues.speaker: Zhi
dialogues.text: A fragment? Let me see... I'm sorry, I've never seen anything like this.

dialogues.speaker: Zhi
dialogues.text: But I think Granny Ruoxin might know. You should go ask her.

dialogues.speaker: Little Xing
dialogues.text: Excuse me, know anything about fragments?

dialogues.speaker: Little Xing
dialogues.text: Fragments? Mm... I don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Little Xing
dialogues.text: You should go ask Granny Ruoxin, she might know.

dialogues.speaker: Little Liu
dialogues.text: Look at this fragment!

dialogues.speaker: Little Liu
dialogues.text: Ah! You scared me! ...What fragment?

dialogues.speaker: Little Liu
dialogues.text: What is it? ...You don't know? Go ask Granny Ruoxin, she knows everything.

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: What do you make of this fragment?

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: A fragment? Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: Lemme see... Wow. I have no idea. I've never seen one of these before.

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: Why don't you go ask Granny Ruoxin?

dialogues.speaker: Pops Kai
dialogues.text: I have this fragment...

dialogues.speaker: Pops Kai
dialogues.text: A fragment, you say? Show me.

dialogues.speaker: Pops Kai
dialogues.text: This writing... or maybe it's not writing at all. I can't read it, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Pops Kai
dialogues.text: Ask the village chief, she's gotta know something.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: ...This is something I never expected to see.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Well, if it's what fate has decreed...

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Forgotten already? Well, I do have a habit of rambling on and on I suppose...

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: If you're looking for fragments connected to the great war, you may have more luck searching in <color=#00E1FFFF>high-altitude</color> places.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Also, you should head <color=#00E1FFFF>west</color> and take a close look nearby the <color=#00E1FFFF>Geo Statues</color>.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Finally, it can't hurt to check the <color=#00E1FFFF>ruins</color> in this area.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Hahaha... I never said I was sure, now, did I?

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Let's just say that at my age, you sometimes find yourself remembering things that most people have forgotten.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: When I was a child, everybody knew the tale of the Geo Lord suppressing the Chi.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: But some people would say that even the Geo Lord himself couldn't wipe out the Chi completely, and so Geo Statues were used to press it down, slowly crushing it to death over time.

response.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
response.text: Haha. But of course, it's just an old story. If there was really a chance the Chi is still alive, we would hardly feel safe living here in Qingce Village.
